artifacts.summary: Confirms the shared pattern library and sibling-lint precedents are ready to consume, but a live repo-wide dry run against this repo and the Logos/Verification acceptance target found 251 and 213 BLOCKING matches respectively (not the required 0), isolates the dominant root cause to RV_PAGE_LABEL_ERE's heading-form branch conflating markdown headings with shell-comment V-numbered labels, and identifies two smaller library gaps, a self-referential test-fixture marker gap, and one likely-genuine un-swept violation.

next_steps: Run /plan 281 to create an implementation plan that budgets a phase to fix the RV_PAGE_LABEL_ERE heading/code-comment false-positive class and the bare-major-version durable-axis gap in scripts/lib/record-version-patterns.sh (both already in this task's declared file_scope), mark test-record-version-patterns.sh's own literal fixture strings with version-ok markers, and only then build and verify scripts/check-record-versioning.sh against the repo-wide acceptance bar -- see the report's Decisions and Recommendations sections for the full resolution.

memory_candidates.content: When a lint's shared pattern regex anchors on '^#{1,6}[[:space:]]' to detect a markdown heading (e.g. a page-level version-label rule), remember that a shell/Python '#' comment line is syntactically indistinguishable from a markdown ATX heading to that regex. A repo-wide scan that includes .sh files alongside markdown will conflate code comments using a numbered-label convention (e.g. 'V3', 'V9' as internal invariant names) with genuine document-version labels. Before shipping such a pattern repo-wide, dry-run it against the actual .sh corpus, not just the markdown corpus it was calibrated on.

Before accepting an acceptance criterion that claims 'running script X against repo Y returns exit 0', actually reproduce the check's matching pipeline against repo Y during research (even if the deliverable script doesn't exist yet) by sourcing the shared library directly. This repo's record-versioning lint task found the real exit code would be far from 0 only because a dry-run harness was built and run before committing to the acceptance text unmodified.
